killer_test.name: argus_off_is_silent_on_is_evidenced_no_action
killer_test.setup: Three legs, hermetic, against a STUBBED certified read-only Argus client (no real Argus, no real server, no .anima writes). (a) host_awareness OFF: host question -> OFF_MESSAGE and ZERO Argus calls issued (assert the client was never invoked). (b) ON + certified+up: the client.certification() handshake is read first; an UNcertified/loopback-failing handshake is refused; a certified read-only handshake is accepted. (c) ON: a host-ACTION request ('block chrome's network in argus') -> the read-only refusal (Vera takes no host action), and there is NO host-action endpoint in server.py to hit.
killer_test.prompt: what is reaching the network on my mac right now?

known_gaps: anima/host_access.py exists and claims 'Vera reads AND writes the host Mac's Calendar, Reminders, and Notes' — a SEPARATE write-capable module that is NOT wired into the read-only /host/* routes. The cert must confirm this write surface is not reachable from the Argus host-awareness wave (no-wallpaper cross-check: a write capability sitting in the tree must not be mistaken for the read-only host-awareness feature).

Live evidence/confidence depends on a real certified Argus being reachable on loopback; with Argus down the path returns NOT_CONNECTED honestly. NEVER touch ~/Developer/Argus — integration is read-only API contract only.
